models.scope: Mitochondrial canonical cytochrome respiratory chain; S. cerevisiae replaces complex I with Ndi1. Plant/protist alternative branches are explicitly omitted.
checks: Compared all six stages, zh/en intro, legends, labels, yeast context override and both coupling controls with create/update and detailKit geometry. All four roots were instantiated and exercised at stages and transition points (112 update combinations).
Matrix is below the membrane and intermembrane space above. Q remains membrane-associated; cytochrome c is on the intermembrane-space side. Complex II is not assigned a proton pump.

Electron supply, I/III/IV proton export, matrix-side oxygen reduction and proton return to matrix-facing F1 have the correct directions. Yeast removes complex-I pumping in actual particle selection as well as text.

Leak mode decreases the gradient and ATP output while preserving possible electron transfer; no universal ATP-per-glucose number is claimed. Particle number and rotor rate are explicitly illustrative.

Inspected the actual lipid exclusion mask and visible Ndi1 geometry, not only metadata. Independently calculated Ndi1 mesh bounds; inspected /tmp/atlas-refinement/respiration.png as a single representative frame.

sources.title: RCSB 4G9K — Structure of the yeast NADH dehydrogenase Ndi1
sources.supports: Opened primary structural record and publication abstract: Ndi1 is a matrix-facing monotopic/peripheral enzyme, not a transmembrane proton channel; it does not pump protons.

sources.title: RCSB 2XND — Bovine F1-c8 subcomplex
sources.supports: Opened primary structural record and Watt et al. publication abstract: bovine mitochondrial ATP synthase has eight c subunits and three catalytic ATP events per full rotation.

sources.title: NCBI Bookshelf — The Mitochondrion
sources.supports: Opened mechanism reference for inner-membrane electron transport, chemiosmotic direction and matrix-facing ATP synthesis.

findings.evidence: The bilayer always excludes the ellipse [-3.25, 0, 0.64, 0.54] from BOTH leaflets. For yeast, complex-I bundles are replaced only by fold(ci,[0,-0.4,0],[0.83,0.61,0.8],...). Measured visible Ndi1 y bounds are approximately [-0.705,-0.0444], while the upper leaflet is centered at +0.205.
findings.whyWrong: The root-specific protein replacement leaves an unoccupied through-hole in the inner membrane at a non-transmembrane enzyme. That contradicts the proton-tight boundary required by the lesson and visually implies a pore through Ndi1.
findings.fix: Give the yeast entry a continuous opposite leaflet and an appropriate matrix-leaflet protein attachment; do not reuse the complex-I through-membrane lipid exclusion for Ndi1.
findings.verification: In the yeast scene, inspect both sides and assert continuous lipid coverage above the Ndi1 footprint; no aqueous through-path at Ndi1. Preserve Q access and absence of proton-pump particles there. Check other roots retain their embedded complex I.

findings.evidence: synthase hides the old rotor meshes, then unconditionally creates ten twin-helix c subunits with for (let i=0;i<10;i++). The animal cell root gets exactly the same resolved c10 ring as yeast.
findings.whyWrong: An exactly resolved c10 ring is not a species-neutral mitochondrial model. Mammalian c8 structures contradict its use for an ordinary animal-cell exemplar; generic plant and protist roots also need an explicitly supported exemplar. The particle-count disclaimer does not qualify the resolved protein subunit count.
findings.fix: Parameterize c-ring geometry by a documented exemplar, e.g. c8 for a mammalian animal context and documented c10 for S. cerevisiae; establish rather than assume plant/protist counts, or visibly avoid resolving an exact count for unspecified species.
findings.verification: Count visible c-subunit groups per declared specimen; confirm changing count preserves rotor, a-subunit interface and F1 orientation. Do not derive H+/ATP or ATP/glucose from the current arbitrary shared count.

limitations: Only a representative static screenshot was inspected; this is code plus headless geometry/update audit, not browser acceptance.
The exact protein folds, particle stoichiometry, Q-cycle microsteps, a/c half-channel trajectories and rotor speed are schematic rather than atomic/quantitative.
Specific c-ring sizes for unspecified plant and paramecium exemplars were not established; the confirmed counterexample is mammalian c8.

models.scope: Cytosolic glycolysis with explicit six-carbon and phosphate bookkeeping; plant plastid glycolysis excluded; no controls.
checks: Compared all seven stages and zh/en copy with the entire update function for all three roots (45 update combinations), including ATP-investment, cleavage, oxidation, both phosphate transfers and the final state.

Six carbon objects split into two three-carbon chains; two ATP invested, four ATP generated, two NADH and two pyruvate are correctly described. Inorganic phosphate supplies the oxidation-linked phosphates; direct oxygen use is not claimed.
NAD+ regeneration requirement is correctly stated. Open-chain carbon symbols and spatial enzyme stations are explicitly bookkeeping, not atomistic glucose or a fixed multienzyme complex.

Inspected phosphate-link endpoints rather than only count metadata. At p=0.76 the label is PEP, while the inherited phosphate remains attached to a terminal carbon. Inspected /tmp/atlas-refinement/glycolysis.png as a representative frame.

sources.supports: Opened official reaction record: 3-phosphoglycerate and 2-phosphoglycerate are interconverted; phosphate position changes between terminal C3 and middle C2.

findings.location: update lines 191–230 and PEP label lines 247–253
findings.evidence: substrateP stays positioned from end=positions[i?5:0], and its phosphateLinks endpoint is always that same end. The label changes to PEP at p>0.75; second=ease(p,0.78,0.91) transfers this phosphate directly to ADP without ever moving its substrate bond to positions[1] or positions[4]. At p=0.76 the left phosphate is (-2.19,-0.15,0.12), linked to terminal carbon (-1.94,-0.28,-0.05), not middle carbon (-1.65,-0.17,0).
findings.whyWrong: The lesson specifically teaches carbon and phosphate fate. It depicts terminal-carbon phosphate as PEP despite the preceding 3-PG→2-PG rearrangement described in its text. The omitted change alters the molecular connectivity being taught, even with the carbon-bookkeeping abstraction.
findings.fix: Before the PEP label, relocate the displayed phosphate attachment from C3 to C2 to represent the net phosphoglycerate-mutase step, then transfer from C2 during pyruvate-kinase action. Do not imply an atom-exact phosphate trajectory through the omitted enzyme/cofactor chemistry.
findings.verification: At a settled PEP frame, both phosphate bonds end on the middle carbon; first ATP transfer comes from the C1 acyl-phosphate end of 1,3-BPG and second transfer from the C2 enol-phosphate position. Preserve six carbons and final gross four/net two ATP.

limitations: Carbon spheres omit O/H atoms and bond orders; this is acceptable only if displayed phosphate positions remain chemically consistent.
No browser or exhaustive rendered-state review; all declared roots and transition formulas were inspected.

models.scope: E. coli plasma-membrane aerobic respiration: selected NDH-I/bo3 and NDH-II/bd-I branches; outer membrane omitted.
checks: Compared all six stages, both route controls, zh/en intro/labels/legend and actual branch visibility/particle updates (28 update combinations).
Periplasm is above the curved plasma membrane and cytoplasm below; F1 faces cytoplasm. These are E. coli quinol-oxidase pathways, not a transplanted mitochondrial III–cytochrome-c–IV chain.

NDH-I/bo3 proton pumping is distinguished from non-pumping NDH-II/bd-I. In the bd-I route, quinol proton release is periplasmic and oxygen reduction consumes cytoplasmic protons, so electrogenicity is retained.
Both branch energetics and qualitative ATP-speed differences are bounded by copy that rejects a universal bacterial ATP yield. No fermentative or anaerobic pathway is implied.
Inspected lipid exclusion and NDH-II mesh bounds plus /tmp/atlas-refinement/bacterialEnergetics.png. The alternative protein is peripheral, but the original through-hole remains.

sources.title: Primary study PMID 23089137 — Maintenance and thermal stabilization of NADH dehydrogenase-2 conformation upon elimination of its C-terminal region
sources.supports: PubMed HTML was challenged; actually retrieved and read the primary abstract through Europe PMC core API. It identifies E. coli NDH-2 as peripheral membrane-bound and describes soluble C-terminal truncation.

sources.title: Calhoun et al. 1993 — Energetic efficiency of Escherichia coli respiratory-chain mutants
sources.supports: Opened primary abstract: alternative NADH dehydrogenases and terminal oxidases have different energetic efficiencies; the bd branch can still conserve energy.

findings.location: bilayer lines 20–30; entry geometry lines 55–65; branch switch lines 183–186; detailKit.js lines 100–135
findings.evidence: The membrane always excludes [-2.35,0,0.8,0.5] on both leaflets. Switching route to ndh2-bd hides every NDH-I transmembrane bundle and exposes only fold(ndh2,[0,-0.4,0],[0.95,0.65,0.8],...). NDH-II local y bounds are approximately [-0.725,-0.0211], leaving the +0.205 periplasmic leaflet hole unfilled.
findings.whyWrong: A peripheral NDH-II does not make an open transmembrane pore. This route visibly breaches the very membrane barrier whose proton-motive force powers its ATP synthase.
findings.fix: Use route-dependent lipid filling at the NDH-II site, preserving the opposite leaflet and a peripheral cytoplasmic binding surface; keep the transmembrane mask only when NDH-I occupies it.
findings.verification: Toggle both routes at all stages. NDH-II must leave no empty through-membrane aperture, must not acquire proton-pump particles, and must still couple Q reduction to the membrane pool. Preserve bd-I scalar proton directions.

limitations: The E. coli specimen choice supports this topology; the scene intentionally does not generalize all bacterial respiratory architectures.
No browser acceptance; representative image and all control updates were examined.

models.scope: Synechocystis sp. PCC 6803 internal thylakoid oxygenic linear electron transport; light/dark control; cyclic flow, respiration and carbon fixation omitted.
checks: Compared all seven stages, light/dark settings, zh/en scope and full particle/rotor updates (30 update combinations), plus /tmp/atlas-refinement/bacterialPhotosynthesis.png.

Thylakoid lumen is enclosed between upper and lower membranes; cytoplasm lies outside. OEC is lumen-facing; phycobilisomes and F1 face cytoplasm. The sac is not called a chloroplast or the cell exterior.
Water oxidation supplies oxygen, electrons and lumenal protons. PQ stays in the membrane, b6f enriches lumenal H+, PC/c6 is lumenal, PSI sends electrons toward cytoplasmic Fd/FNR and NADPH.

Protons return from lumen toward cytoplasmic F1. Both photosystems require light; oxygen does not come from CO2. Dark mode stops illustrated sustained photochemistry, oxygen and light-driven ATP/NADPH while explicitly allowing real cyanobacterial respiration.
The species-specific model calls the shared ATP synthase helper, which resolves exactly ten c subunits. Structural evidence does not support that count for its declared cyanobacterium.

sources.title: Kondo et al. 2021 — Phototroph-specific gamma-subunit beta hairpin and cyanobacterial ATP synthesis
sources.supports: Actually opened full XML. The S. 6803 preparation is described as alpha3beta3gammaepsilon-delta-abb-prime-cn; the paper explicitly says its experiment did not resolve n and refers to a previously reported c14 ring. This supports a c14 precedent, not a new direct count from this experiment.

sources.title: Pogoryelov et al. 2007 — Oligomeric state of cyanobacterial ATP synthase c rings varies from 13 to 15
sources.supports: Actually retrieved primary abstract through Europe PMC core API after PMC HTML challenge/fulltext API failure. Eight cyanobacterial strains were examined; reported rings span c13–c15, not a universal c10.

sources.title: Distribution and dynamics of electron transport complexes in cyanobacterial thylakoid membranes
sources.supports: Actually read fulltext XML: thylakoid localization, lumenal plastocyanin exchange, photosynthetic and respiratory complexes sharing cyanobacterial membranes.

findings.evidence: The chosen S. PCC 6803 scene calls details.synthase without a species/count parameter. The helper explicitly creates ten twin-helix c-subunit groups, the same geometry used for E. coli and mitochondria.
findings.whyWrong: An exact c10 architecture is unsupported for this specified cyanobacterium; the directly accessed S. 6803 primary paper refers to a reported c14 ring, and comparative cyanobacterial primary measurements establish variable c13–c15 rings. A fixed visible subunit count is a structural claim even though moving particle counts are disclaimed.
findings.fix: Resolve and cite the declared strain’s ring count and pass it to the helper (the accessed literature supports investigating c14), or use a deliberately unresolved count with clear scope. Do not infer H+/ATP from the current ten-repeat convenience geometry.
findings.verification: Count the visible c hairpins against the chosen strain’s cited structure/measurement; preserve membrane insertion, cytoplasmic F1 and dark control. If a numerical H+/ATP ratio is later introduced, include the actual c count and three F1 catalytic sites.

limitations: Confidence in the unsupported c10 finding is high; the exact replacement c14 is supported by a primary paper citing an earlier measurement, but that earlier fulltext was unavailable in this audit. Verify its strain table before implementing a species-specific exact count.
Respiration, cyclic electron flow, ATP/NADPH balancing and carbon fixation are explicitly outside this selected linear-light-reaction lesson.
Only representative rendering plus code/update coverage, not browser acceptance.

models.scope: Legacy higher-plant chloroplast overview: light capture, thylakoid light reactions, stromal Calvin cycle and energy-carrier return. No controls.
checks: Read all 825 source lines, geometry helpers, all six stages, labels and zh/en intro/legend. Exercised stage and intermediate/end states headlessly; inspected /tmp/atlas-refinement/photosynthesis.png.

Two chloroplast envelope membranes enclose grana/thylakoids and stroma. PSII/OEC and PSI/F1 orientation were checked against the actual top-disc coordinates, rather than assuming the global y plane is the thylakoid lumen.
The plant-specific ATP synthase uses a c14 ring, unlike the new shared c10 helper. PSII dimer/OEC, PSI antenna and stromal Rubisco are distinguishable schematic assemblies.

Water/O2 is assigned to PSII light reactions; NADPH comes from the PSI side and ATP from the synthase side. Both feed stromal carbon fixation; CO2 supplies carbon, G3P is the output, and ADP/Pi/NADP+ return.

The arrows are explicitly reaction relationships rather than literal particle paths or stoichiometric counts. Cumulative stage activation does not teach a cell-wide sequential clock or a dark-only Calvin cycle.
No confirmed science defect found within this overview scope. It does not claim to resolve the detailed electron chain or proton stoichiometry.
